test_title: SSC GD Constable (2022) Official Paper (Held On : 24 Jan 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Choose the appropriate meaning of the underlying idiom.

She wants to reach the target __by hook or by crook.__

options.text: By one or the other means

solution:
The correct answer is '**By one or the other means**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined idiom in the sentence is '**by hook or by crook**'. This idiom means to achieve something by any means necessary, using fair means or foul. (चाहे जैसे भी)

 
 
• **Example**: He's determined to get that job **by hook or by crook**.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct meaning of '**by hook or by crook**' is '**By one or the other means**'.

Therefore, the correct answer is- "**Option 1**".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2: '**With all of one’s (her) belongings**' is incorrect because the idiom 'by hook or by crook' has nothing to do with possessing all belongings.
 
• Option 3: '**Without deception**' is also not correct as 'by hook or by crook' doesn't necessarily imply fairness or transparency, rather it even allows foul means if necessary.
 
• Option 4: '**Very rapidly**' is incorrect as the idiom 'by hook or by crook' primarily signifies the determination to achieve something, irrespective of the speed of the process.
